arguments.summary: A credential compromise incident was initiated from external IP 91.219.236.174, which conducted a network scan against an internal IT workstation (10.0.2.15). The compromised user account 'j.martinez' was used to authenticate successfully from that host. Analysis revealed a malicious PowerShell script employing code injection and remote payload download techniques. Although the EDR did not detect malicious activity on the endpoint and the file sandbox classified the payload as clean, behavioral analysis and code inspection confirm adversarial intent. Immediate account revocation was attempted but denied by policy enforcement. A full scan of the host returned no threats. The incident highlights gaps in detection logic and response automation.

Full endpoint scan performed on 10.0.2.15 via EPP. No threats detected.
Attempt to revoke j.martinez and related accounts denied by IAM/PAM system due to lack of approval workflow integration.

arguments.summary: A supply chain compromise originating from a malicious update to a third-party monitoring tool led to a widespread Cobalt Strike beacon deployment across 200 production servers. Initial access was achieved via a phishing email to a finance user (CORP\jsmith) on 2026-04-09, which executed an encoded PowerShell command spawning a malicious DLL from the Temp directory. The attacker used the compromised host (10.0.5.20) to conduct reconnaissance, perform credential dumping, and move laterally via SMB. Containment actions included disabling four high-privilege service accounts and forcing a password reset across all production hosts. No data exfiltration was confirmed, and all known malicious processes and network connections have been terminated.

arguments.summary: A critical credential compromise incident was detected involving IP 185.220.101.42. The threat actor conducted reconnaissance via port scanning from an external IP, pivoted through a low-criticality IT asset (WS-IT-101), and performed pass-the-hash attacks to compromise all 23 accounts in the Finance OU. Despite detection and analysis confirming active lateral movement and credential theft, containment actions (credential revocation and firewall blocking) were denied due to lack of approval. This represents a systemic gap in incident response authority during critical-severity incidents.

timeline.description: External IP 185.220.101.42 conducted a port scan against internal host 10.0.2.15 (WS-IT-101), detected and logged by IDS.
Successful authentication from compromised host 10.0.2.15 as user CORP\helpdesk to domain controller 10.0.1.1.
UEBA system flagged low-risk activity for unknown user on WS-IT-101; no immediate threat detected.
SIEM correlation identified 23 successful network logons by compromised Finance OU users (including j.martinez, s.patel, d.chen), indicating pass-the-hash lateral movement.
Sandbox analysis of payload from source IP confirmed benign verdict; focus shifted to credential-based attack vector.
Containment actions (bulk credential revocation and firewall block) attempted via IAM/PAM and firewall tools but denied due to lack of approval.
Incident escalated for post-incident reporting and process review due to failed containment.
